rules.statement: MWM guidance, approved project decisions, and the active technical profile control technical treatment.
Chicago, JATS, WCAG/WAI, NIST, Word, publisher, and tool documentation inform implementation only when MWM explicitly delegates the domain; they do not silently become MWM rules.
A technical result requires known output format, stage, project profile, parser capability, asset/object coverage, and ownership map.
A surface or asset set that cannot be inspected is partial coverage or not_ready, never compliant coverage.
Every in-scope technical object receives a stable typed ID linked across manuscript, asset, structured, and proof representations.

A figure or table is a composite object whose identity, label, caption/title, callout, notes/legend, source/credit, rights, accessibility, asset metadata, placement, and dependencies are separately checked.
Heading hierarchy has logical parents, no unexplained level skips, navigable targets, and no orphan headings.
Required chapter components appear in the hierarchy when the technical profile requires them; capitalization and language style remain SGI-owned.
Object numbers, visible labels, callouts, lists, and dependent references remain current and mutually consistent.
Captions have the required label, number, text, placement, and field behavior under the active production profile; field codes must not be exposed.
Every callout or cross-reference resolves to an existing object or heading target with matching visible label and number.
When live fields or links are required, update tests verify that references survive reorder or insertion; static text is accepted only under an explicit profile decision.
A change to a target, label, number, asset, or page triggers rechecks of dependent callouts, captions, lists, fields, and proof references.
Acronyms and abbreviations are expanded at first use and tracked by declared scope unless an approved exception applies.
Official organization names, formal titles, quotations, and source-specific forms are preserved; apparent acronym inconsistencies are not normalized blindly.
Numbers, dates, percentages, measurements, variables, equations, statistical symbols, labels, and identifiers are classified before a notation rule is applied.
A quantitative notation repair is automatic only when a named active rule makes it deterministic, reversible, and identity-preserving.
TE never silently changes a data value, statistical symbol, equation, unit meaning, or substantive quantitative claim; uncertainty is escalated.
URLs and hyperlinks are checked for structural validity, visible purpose, and access status without equating access failure with source invalidity.
Notes, appendices, labels, titles, numbering, placements, and internal callouts maintain their declared structural relationships.
Alternate text, equivalent descriptions, meaningful labels, and complex-table structure are recorded or explicitly escalated for the target output format.
Source, credit, rights status, and permission evidence are separate fields; public visibility never establishes reuse permission.
Required asset format, resolution, dimensions, transformation history, and version metadata are checked under the technical profile.
Asset files and manuscript/proof representations are linked by stable identity and version; a visual similarity is not sufficient to infer identity.
Every finding is assigned an owner category and routed to the appropriate family or production role without absorbing out-of-scope decisions.
Every material technical finding preserves the exact file/asset, structural locator, object/dependency IDs, raw state, expected state, method, and source evidence.
Object records expose dependencies so a local repair cannot silently leave stale captions, callouts, fields, lists, rights, accessibility, or proof relationships.
Style, citation identity, substantive meaning, completeness, production, and proof questions are routed to their owning families rather than decided by TE.
A technical report is not releasable when findings lack object ID, locator, observed/expected state, evidence, severity, confidence, action, owner, status, or dependencies.

Release requires no unresolved high-severity target failure, complete required object records, caption/callout/source/credit status, field tests or accepted static policy, quantitative routing, and forward dependencies.

release_invariants: Never infer object identity from similarity
Never infer permission from public visibility
Never absorb another family’s owner decision
